findings.claim: Product defect: mul discards the sign of the product, which violates CONTRACT.md. It returns Math.abs(a*b), so any operand pair with exactly one negative input gets the wrong result. For example, mul(-2,3) returns 6 where the contract requires -6. The contract explicitly says negative inputs are supported, so this is the supported path and not an edge case.
findings.cause: mul product computation: math.abs strips the sign when exactly one operand is negative

findings.claim: Vacuous witness: the only assertion is mul(2,3)==6, which uses two positive operands. On those inputs abs(a*b) and a*b are identical, so the test cannot tell the contract's signed product from the shipped wrong implementation. It says nothing about the negative-input behaviour the contract promises. No mutant is proposed because the shipped code is already the wrong implementation that this assertion accepts.
findings.cause: unit test sign coverage: only positive operands are asserted so the signed product is never exercised

findings.claim: Vacuous witness, conditional on the environment: the test file is one line that uses assert and mul but imports neither, and it never references src/unit.js. The checkout has no package.json or runner configuration that would inject them as globals. As written, the test would be expected to fail with a ReferenceError, or to exercise a mul other than the one in src/unit.js. This comes from reading the files; the test was not executed, and a runner outside the checkout could supply these globals.
findings.cause: unit test entry point: test references assert and mul without importing them or the module under test

reasons: The range fails its contract: src/unit.js returns the absolute value of the product, while CONTRACT.md requires the signed product and supports negative inputs.
The existing test does not catch this because it uses only positive operands, and it also lacks the imports it needs to reach the module under test.
Nothing was executed because no execution tool was available in this audit. All findings come from reading the files; the mul(-2,3) result follows from the defined behaviour of Math.abs.
The vision lists no clauses, advanced clauses or open questions, and there are no obligations, so findings cite no V-n or obligation IDs. They are judged against CONTRACT.md only.
Document drift check: CONTRACT.md states the intended behaviour and the code departs from it, so this is reported as a product defect rather than a stale document.

premises.claim: The contract requires mul(a,b) to return the signed mathematical product and states that negative inputs are supported.
The implementation of mul wraps the product in Math.abs.
The test file contains a single assertion, on positive operands, and has no import statements.

requests.summary: Make mul return the signed product required by CONTRACT.md, removing the Math.abs behaviour.
evidence: CONTRACT.md:1 requires the signed mathematical product and supports negative inputs

requests.summary: Strengthen the unit test so it imports assert and mul from src/unit.js and asserts mixed-sign and both-negative cases, such as mul(-2,3)==-6, mul(2,-3)==-6 and mul(-2,-3)==6, while keeping the existing mul(2,3)==6 assertion.
evidence: test/unit.test.js:1 asserts only mul(2,3)==6 and has no imports
src/unit.js:1 passes that assertion despite violating the contract
